lines.text: Case open!
Hey! That's not fair! The cricket box is locked!
The lock needs a code with four digits.
Today's case: a code hidden in thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
Digits are the numbers zero to nine.
Place value means a digit's place shows its size.
Like at the canteen. Ten one-dollar coins make one ten-dollar note.
Mabel left a clue made of number blocks.
Big cubes are thousands. Flats are hundreds.
Long sticks are tens. Little cubes are ones.
Three cubes, five sticks, two little cubes. It's three, five, two!
But the lock has four dials.
Let's not guess. Let's test.
Can you find the hundreds? Point to them.
There are no flats. So there are no hundreds.
Which code opens the lock?
A. Three, five, two, zero.
B. Three, zero, five, two.
Pause and think.
Put each block in its place. Three thousands.
No hundreds, so we write zero.
Five tens. Two ones.
Zero holds the hundreds place. It's B!
Oh! The zero was hiding!
Let's count the blocks to check.
Three thousand. Three thousand and fifty. Three thousand and fifty-two.
Three, zero, five, two.
Case solved!
Look! A real cricket!
Not that kind of cricket!
Remember. Zero holds a place when there are none.
Say it with me. Zero holds the place.
Try it at home. Make a secret code with a zero.
Next case: counting to ten, one acorn at a time.
